subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A random variable X has the following probability distribution: X = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; P(X = xᵢ) = 0, k, 2k, 2k, 3k, k², 2k², 7k² + k. Find (i) k (ii) the mean (iii) P(0 < X < 5).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find k, the mean and P(0 < X < 5) from this table — what equation gives k, why one root is rejected, what you add for the mean, and which values of X the probability covers.
insider_note: Σ P(X = xᵢ) = 1 carries the first three marks and here it is a quadratic, 10k² + 9k − 1 = 0 — the lone k inside 7k² + k is the term most often dropped; k = −1 must be rejected in writing, because a probability cannot be negative.

steps.label: Find k
steps.margin_note: Three marks. The sum of the probabilities is a QUADRATIC in k this time: 10k² + 9k − 1 = 0. Factor it — (10k − 1)(k + 1) — and reject k = −1 in words, because a probability cannot be negative. The rejection is a marked line, not a footnote.

recall.must_convey: That the probabilities add to 1, giving 10k² + 9k − 1 = 0, which factors as (10k − 1)(k + 1) = 0; k = −1 is rejected because a probability cannot be negative, so k = 1/10.
accept: the probabilities add to one giving ten k squared plus nine k minus one equals zero, factor it, reject minus one, k is one by ten
sum of P equals one is a quadratic in k, solve it and drop the negative root
ten k square plus nine k minus one is zero so k is one by ten or minus one and minus one is not allowed
probabilities kalipithe one, quadratic vastundi, minus one reject chesi k one by ten
solve the quadratic from sigma P equals one and keep only the positive k

steps.why: Adding the k² terms and the k terms separately turns the rule ΣP = 1 into a quadratic, and a quadratic has two roots. Only one of them can be a probability, so the rejection is part of the answer, not a remark.
common_mistakes: Missing the k inside 7k² + k, so the k terms add to 8k instead of 9k.
Writing k = 1/10 without saying why k = −1 is rejected.

steps.label: Find the mean
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Mean μ = Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ). The x = 0 term is 0, so start from 1(k). Collect the k terms (30k) and the k² terms (66k²) separately, then put k = 1/10: 3 + 0.66 = 3.66.

recall.must_convey: That the mean is Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ) = 30k + 66k² = 3 + 0.66 = 3.66.
accept: mean is sigma x times P of x which is thirty k plus sixty six k squared equals three point six six
multiply each value by its probability, collect the k and k squared terms, put k equal to one by ten
mu equals thirty k plus sixty six k square which is three point six six
prathi x ni probability tho multiply chesi add cheste thirty k plus sixty six k square, mean three point six six
the mean comes to three point six six

steps.why: The mean is the weighted average of the values. Collecting like terms in k before substituting keeps the arithmetic to two short products at the end instead of eight fractions.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 7·k part of 7(7k² + k), so the k terms add to 23k.
Including the x = 0 term as something other than zero.

steps.label: Find P(0 < X < 5)
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. 0 < X < 5 means X = 1, 2, 3, 4 — both ends are EXCLUDED. Add those four probabilities: k + 2k + 2k + 3k = 8k = 4/5. Including X = 0 changes nothing here (its probability is 0), but including X = 5 is wrong.

recall.must_convey: That P(0 < X < 5) is the sum of the probabilities for X = 1, 2, 3, 4 (strict inequalities), which is 8k = 4/5.
accept: P of zero less than X less than five is P of one plus P of two plus P of three plus P of four which is eight k equals four by five
add the probabilities for X equal to one two three and four to get four by five
strict inequality so take one to four only, eight k is four by five
zero and five ni vadili one nunchi four varaku probabilities add cheste eight k, four by five
the probability is eight k which is four fifths

steps.why: The event 0 < X < 5 is a set of values of X, and its probability is the sum of the probabilities of those values. Reading the inequality signs correctly is the whole step.
common_mistakes: Including X = 5 (k²) because 5 appears in the question.
